title: Safe Clinical AI
summary: AI systems reliable enough for medical practice — not just impressive on benchmarks.
argument: A mistake in a language model demo is annoying. A mistake in clinical decision support can cause direct harm. This asymmetry demands a different standard of reliability — one that accounts for distribution shift, edge cases, and the need for honest uncertainty communication.

This program studies what building clinically reliable AI actually requires: systems that fail predictably, communicate uncertainty honestly, and remain consistent across the full distribution of patients and conditions in real medical practice.
currentWork: Reviewing validation methodologies across existing clinical AI deployments and building a taxonomy of distribution shift patterns specific to clinical data.
futureDirection: Developing practical frameworks for uncertainty communication in clinical decision support — surfacing model confidence in a form that is actionable for practitioners.
